speaker: Doctor
text: I see; can you tell me exactly what you experience when you wake up frightened? Do you recall any dreams, and do you remember them after waking?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; since she isn't confused afterward and is easily consoled, this sounds less like night terrors. To differentiate between nightmares and other sleep disorders, do you remember the specific content of the frightening dreams she has before waking up?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.
